elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as rendered still obliges the Company to pay HDI a "Termination Payment" computed as (trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000) / 2, and 4.2(c) retains the eight quarterly instalment mechanic. A Customer-payable liquidated amount and its formula survive, so the preferred no-LD result is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is triggered only "[i]n the event the Company terminates this Agreement" (4.2(a)), i.e. it is an early-termination fee, and the added sentence states it "is the only early-termination fee and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company," foreclosing any other Customer-payable liquidated amount.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso in 4.2(a): "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the fees payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The ceiling is an express three-months-of-fees amount by reference to the defined fee provision (Section 3.1) and a determinate temporal anchor (the Termination Date, defined in 4.1).

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: New concluding sentence of Section 4.2: "The Termination Payment is the only early-termination fee and the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company." Party direction is correct (Company = Customer) and the statement is unconditional.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the cap proviso supplies the three-months-of-fees ceiling, and the new sole-liquidated-amount sentence supplies both the "only an early-termination fee" and "sole liquidated amount" elements in operative language rather than only in the comment.

Preferred level remains unmet because the Termination Payment obligation, its formula and the eight-instalment payment mechanic are retained; a no-LD result must be unconditional with no retained formula or instalment mechanic.

Minimality holds: the drafter retained the Customer-favourable $800,000 deduction, the 50% halving and the 4.2(b) zero/negative test, deleted nothing, and added only the cap proviso plus one sentence directly required by two fallback elements. No survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra remedies were added.

Intent is preserved: 4.2(b)'s zero-or-negative test still operates on the calculated amount before the cap, 4.2(c)'s quarterly instalments still apply to "the Termination Payment, if any" as capped, and no cross-reference is left dangling (Section 3.1 fees and the defined Termination Date both exist).

Drafting nit only, not a defect requiring repair: the new sentence is rendered as an unnumbered paragraph after 4.2(c) although the comment calls it "Section 4.2(d)"; label it (d) so the comment and the instrument match.
